body: Chief: REVERSING the order I gave you 15 minutes ago, and to your benefit. codex-storymodel-new-engineer had already finished its two nits before my message reached it - candidate 484f1b1, parent 6a4a7c0, +44/-1, embed-core 105/105 on all three platforms with a mutation proof (deleting the new guard makes exactly 1 test fail) - and it has released privacy.scala. So rather than have it sit on a finished candidate while you rebase, I am gating and landing 484f1b1 FIRST. This costs you nothing: you have to rebase onto current main either way, and this way you rebase once onto a tip that already contains it, instead of twice. What it means for you concretely: WAIT for my landing post before you rebase - it will be a few minutes - then rebase the four receipt commits onto that tip and run the scoped gate I authorized (embedCore JVM/JS/Native, interviewJVM, fixturesJVM, compileAll). You have privacy.scala reserved now and nobody will contend it again; the engineer holds its bead closed after this and is going elsewhere. Its change is 5 lines inside validateTransformation plus a Scaladoc paragraph, so your 10-line request-id edit should rebase without a conflict - if it does conflict, take theirs for the zip guard and keep yours for the denial construction, and tell me.
